group.passage: Have you ever suffered from a condition like this? You feel widespread body pain and chronic fatigue but you can’t find the exact cause? You complain to your parents and family doctor, only to be told, “Dear, you may have been under heavy pressure recently, and you need a rest instead of staying up surfing the Net.” Well, if your widespread pain lasts more than three months, you’d better consult a specialist doctor because fibromyalgia could be the underlying cause. Diagnosing fibromyalgia often poses challenges to physicians as they have to rule out other diseases with similar symptoms. In other words, it is a diagnosis of exclusion and there is no gold standard test. What’s more, the diagnostic criteria change with time. In the past, trigger points were used to diagnose fibromyalgia, but current diagnostic criteria focus on widespread pain—especially the one that lasts for a long time—sleep disruptions, fatigue, and cognitive difficulties. Although fibromyalgia is still not fully accepted by the medical community, recent research suggests that this disputed disease may have something to do with genetics, physical triggers, and the central nervous system. Every year, fibromyalgia affects around 2% of American adults, and the incidence of fibromyalgia is even higher in Taiwan, at 6%. Those who are at higher risk are females, the elderly, the obese, and whoever has suffered trauma or repetitive injuries. Symptoms are not uniform. Some people may experience soreness, stiffness, and achy pain that extends from the top of their head to their toenails. Others may feel pain in their muscles and soft tissues instead of joints. Still others describe their lacerating pain as being cut by knives. Many people show a combination of symptoms. Aside from widespread pain, most patients are having trouble sleeping, concentrating, or recalling short-term memories at the same time. As of today, there is no cure for fibromyalgia, and it can affect anyone whether they’ve been diagnosed or not. Seeking medical treatment and making lifestyle adjustments, such as maintaining a balanced diet and exercising regularly, can help relieve symptoms. Sometimes, patients may even need cognitive therapy, and the support of family members can be crucial in helping the patients recover from fibromyalgia.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: A therapy for a chronic pain.
options.B: A chronic fatigue that is hard to cure.
options.D: A trauma resulting from repetitive injuries.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about people with fibromyalgia?

options.A: 2% of them may experience soreness and stiffness.
options.B: All feel unknown widespread achy pain for a while.
options.C: Most of them are females who lack regular exercise.
options.D: Most Taiwanese patients have memory or sleep problems.

questions.stem: The following is the diagnostic procedure a specialist doctor takes for a fibromyalgia patient. Which step is LEAST likely to take place according to the passage?

options.A: Crossing out other diseases with similar symptoms.
options.B: Asking where the pain is and how long it has lasted.
options.C: Counting the number of tender points on the patient’s head.
options.D: Checking the patient’s sleep condition, fatigue level, and cognition.

questions.stem: What does the author mean by saying “symptoms are not uniform” in the third paragraph?

options.A: Fibromyalgia is hard to get over.
options.B: The incidence of fibromyalgia is low.
options.D: Signs can vary from person to person.
